# A wire name holding a `$` -- JSON Schema's `$id` and `$ref` -- is decoded and
# written by that name on every target. Kotlin's codec quoted wire names as Go
# does, so `"$id"` was a string template reading a variable `id`, and the
# android build failed.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import json "sngl:json"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

enum Link {
    #[json.identifier("$ref")]
    ref
    inline
}

struct Schema {
    #[json.identifier("$id")]
    id   string
    link Link
}

component page ui.node {
    ui.text(value="schema")
}

func testADollarWireName(t test.Test, c page) {
    match var s = json.decode[Schema](`{"$id":"a","link":"$ref"}`) {
        ok {
            t.assert(s.id == "a" && s.link == Link.ref)
            t.assert(json.encode(s) == `{"$id":"a","link":"$ref"}`)
        }
        failed { t.assert(s.message == "") }
    }
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
